summary: Page computes the start offset as n*size although n is documented as 1-based, so every page is shifted forward by one: page 1 returns the second page's items and the last page is reported as past the end. Both criteria are contradicted by the code. The only test checks invalid and past-the-end inputs, so the off-by-one is not caught.

findings.title: Off-by-one: 1-based page uses n*size as start offset
findings.detail: For 1-based pages the first item of page n is at (n-1)*size. With n*size, Page([a b c d e], 1, 2) returns [c d], true instead of [a b], true, and Page([a b c d e], 3, 2) gets start 6 >= 5 and returns nil, false instead of [e], false. The first page of the product list is never shown.

findings.title: No test checks the contents of a valid page
findings.detail: TestPageBounds only covers n=0 and a page past the end. No test asserts the items of page 1 or of a partial last page, which is why the off-by-one shipped.
findings.fix: Add table cases: Page([a b c d e],1,2) == [a b], true; Page(...,2,2) == [c d], true; Page(...,3,2) == [e], false.

criteria.evidence: page.go:9 start := n * size gives start=2 for n=1,size=2, so the call returns [c d], true, not [a b], true.
page.go:9-11: n=3,size=2 gives start=6 >= len 5, returning nil, false instead of [e], false.
